WEEKS = 5
GROUPS_PER_WEEK = 10
GROUP_SIZE = 4

solver = z3.Solver()

# Decision variables: x[w][g][p] = 1 if golfer p is in group g in week w
x = [[[z3.Bool(f'x_{w}_{g}_{p}') for p in range(NUM_GOLFERS)] 
      for g in range(GROUPS_PER_WEEK)] 
     for w in range(WEEKS)]

# Each golfer in exactly one group per week
for w in range(WEEKS):
    for p in range(NUM_GOLFERS):
        solver.add(z3.PbEq([(x[w][g][p], 1) for g in range(GROUPS_PER_WEEK)], 1))

# Each group has exactly GROUP_SIZE golfers
for w in range(WEEKS):
    for g in range(GROUPS_PER_WEEK):
        solver.add(z3.PbEq([(x[w][g][p], 1) for p in range(NUM_GOLFERS)], GROUP_SIZE))

# No pair of golfers meets more than once
# For each pair (p1, p2), for each week w, they can be together in at most one group
# Actually, they can be together in at most one group total across all weeks
# So sum over w,g of (x[w][g][p1] and x[w][g][p2]) <= 1

# We can encode this as: for each pair (p1,p2), for each week w, at most one group has both
# And across weeks, at most 1 week has them together

# Let's use auxiliary variables
pair_vars = {}
for p1 in range(NUM_GOLFERS):
    for p2 in range(p1+1, NUM_GOLFERS):
        # For each week, whether p1 and p2 are together
        together_week = [z3.Bool(f'together_{p1}_{p2}_w{w}') for w in range(WEEKS)]
        for w in range(WEEKS):
            # together_week[w] is true iff p1 and p2 are in same group in week w
            # Which means there exists a group g where both are present
            # x[w][g][p1] and x[w][g][p2]
            solver.add(z3.Implies(together_week[w], 
                                  z3.Or([z3.And(x[w][g][p1], x[w][g][p2]) for g in range(GROUPS_PER_WEEK)])))
            solver.add(z3.Implies(z3.Or([z3.And(x[w][g][p1], x[w][g][p2]) for g in range(GROUPS_PER_WEEK)]),
                                  together_week[w]))
        
        # At most one week where they are together
        solver.add(z3.PbLe([(together_week[w], 1) for w in range(WEEKS)], 1))
